title: China October fuel-export suspension adds independent refined-product supply stress
net_new_delta: Chinese refiners suspended October oil-product exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau while domestic diesel/gasoil inventories were reported roughly 20 million barrels below the pre-war threshold and gasoline roughly 9 million barrels below. This adds a distinct China supply-security withdrawal channel to the already stressed global refined-product regime.
fact: Reuters reported on 2026-10-01, updated 2026-10-02, that Chinese refiners suspended October oil-product exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau.
PetroChina cancelled some planned October gasoline and jet-fuel cargoes; Zhejiang Petrochemical scheduled no product shipments during the holiday week.
Reuters reported October-November Asian diesel spreads reached a two-week high on expectations Chinese export supply would be absent.
source_claim: Kpler estimated Chinese commercial gasoil/diesel inventories about 20 million barrels below the threshold Beijing uses for export normalization, with gasoline about 9 million barrels short.
Sources said permission after October 7 remained uncertain and depended on domestic inventories and refining output.
model_inference: Add CHINA_REFINED_PRODUCT_EXPORT_WITHDRAWAL as a time-valid supply-security state. It compounds Middle-East and Russian refined-product stress but should not be treated as a permanent export ban or a quantified global shortage until physical October flows confirm it.
affected_assumptions: China can be treated as a stable marginal refined-product export buffer
crude availability adequately proxies refined-product availability
conflicts: China has large refining capacity and exports could resume after the holiday if domestic stocks recover; South Korean refiners may partially cover the gap, though reported spot availability is limited.
unknown: Whether Beijing permits exports after October 7
magnitude of substitution by other Asian refiners
next_decisive_check: After October 7, verify Chinese export permissions and actual diesel/gasoline/jet-fuel loadings, then compare domestic inventories, Asian diesel cracks/spreads, and substitution volumes from South Korea/India.

oracle.finding: China's October product-export suspension creates a distinct refined-product supply-security withdrawal state that compounds existing Russian and Middle-East product scarcity without proving a permanent shortage.

supermesh_x.finding: Reuters source reporting plus Kpler/LSEG physical-flow context supports event discovery; promotion should require post-Oct-7 export permissions and observed cargo loadings rather than policy/source reports alone.
